content:
maria: Hey all — hitting a weird intermittent auth failure in the Kotlin client. Happens only on long-lived streaming requests (NDJSON) and after a redirect. Local repro: 1) call /v1/stream -> 302 -> follows redirect -> sometimes 401 from backend. No proxy in the middle.

devon: Do you have a custom OkHttp Interceptor for Authorization? if so check interceptor ordering vs networkInterceptor. Redirects create a new request and some interceptors are re-run differently. Also, are you using followRedirects=true (default)? headers may be dropped.

maria: Yes we add an AuthInterceptor that adds `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Using default followRedirects. Notably it only fails when response is NDJSON streaming (chunked). Regular non-streaming calls always OK.

sebastian: Two immediate guesses: 1) header drop on redirect as devon said, 2) shading/classloader issue: we recently shaded jackson-core/jackson-databind AND bundled gson for streaming. If two different JsonFactory/JsonParser versions are on the classpath the streaming reader can throw NoSuchMethodError or silently fail in certain code paths.

ryan: FWIW we've seen OkHttp create a new Request on redirect that may not copy a non-proxy Authorization header for security reasons. Solutions: a) use `client.newBuilder().followRedirects(false)` and handle 302+ manually and reattach auth; b) mark the interceptor as a network interceptor (it runs after redirects): `addNetworkInterceptor(authInterceptor)`; c) put token in cookie (not ideal).

maria: Trying addNetworkInterceptor now. Also saw stacktrace in CI: `NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonFactory.createJsonParser(Ljava/io/InputStream;)` which points to conflicting jackson versions. CI log: [ci-bot] build/482 failed with that NoSuchMethodError during unit tests that parse streaming responses.

devon: For the shading problem, in Gradle (shadowJar) relocate packages. Example we use:

```
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'shadowed.com.fasterxml.jackson'
  relocate 'com.google.gson', 'shadowed.com.google.gson'
}
```

But also make sure to exclude transitive duplication from dependencies that bring a different jackson. `dependencyInsight` helps find the culprit: `./gradlew dependencyInsight --configuration runtimeClasspath --dependency jackson-databind`.

sebastian: Another gotcha: when you relocate, ensure any reflective access paths (names in config) are updated; some libs call Jackson classes by FQCN strings. If you relocate but forget to reconfigure, you'll get runtime errors. For our SDK we prefer to shade jackson entirely under `ai.redwood.shaded.jackson` to avoid collisions with customer apps.

maria: After switching to addNetworkInterceptor the redirect case seems more stable in my local. Still worried about the NoSuchMethodError during tests.

ryan: For streaming NDJSON parsing, avoid mapping the full stream to String before parsing. Use `InputStream` -> `InputStreamReader` -> `JsonFactory.createParser(reader)` (jackson) or `JsonReader` for Gson. Example snippet:

```
val parser = jacksonFactory.createParser(InputStreamReader(response.body().byteStream()))
while (!parser.isClosed) {
  val node = mapper.readTree(parser)
  // handle element
}
```

If you convert to `response.body()!!.string()` you force buffering and can mask timing issues and memory blowups.

maria: Good call. Our tests were reading `.string()` then feeding gson JsonReader - switching to `byteStream()` + streaming parser fixed one flaky test. Still have CI failing in another suite with NoSuchMethodError referencing `JsonFactory#createJsonParser(InputStream)` (old API) vs `createParser` (new API).

devon: That exact error means a mix of jackson-core versions (1.x vs 2.x style APIs or older 2.x). Use `./gradlew dependencies` and search. If a transitive lib brings jackson 2.5 and you compiled with 2.13 you'll see missing methods. Force a consistent jackson version in `dependencies` with `implementation('com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core:2.15.2') { force = true }` or use `constraints`.

sebastian: If you can't force the version (enterprise apps sometimes), shading (relocation) is the safer route for the SDK; customers will bring their own jackson and you avoid conflict. Also watch for `service loader` entries and `META-INF` mismatch — shadow plugin can merge service files.

maria: This is super helpful. Action plan: 1) make AuthInterceptor a networkInterceptor for redirects (short-term); 2) change tests to stream via `byteStream()`; 3) run dependencyInsight and either force jackson or add shadow relocation in the client artifact. I'll open a PR with those changes.

ryan: One more thing re retries: OkHttp's automatic retries on connection failures may replay the body only if `RequestBody` is repeatable. For streaming requests you can't re-send the same InputStream -> set `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` or implement idempotency on server to handle replays. Also consider `connectionPool(new ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))` for lots of short-lived streams.

maria: Noted. I'll temporarily disable retry for streaming endpoints.

ci-bot: build 483 started for branch `maria/okhttp-ndjson-fix`

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-kotlin/pull/312 — includes networkInterceptor swap, tests switched to streaming, gradle dependencyInsight output attached in PR. Could reviewers please look at shading approach?

devon: I'll review the PR this afternoon. Quick tip: include a small reproducer in the tests that simulates a 302 redirect + chunked NDJSON to validate the fix.

sebastian: LGTM otherwise. If we go with shading, coordinate with packaging team for the release notes — users need to know we shaded jackson/gson to avoid surprises.

maria: Thanks all, will iterate and ping when CI passes. :+1:
